items.title: Joseph Thomas Interview, 1960-09-29
items.q: The last time I bought reads, Peterson claimed that I should get a two and a half because I'm older and I should use a soft read.

ctx.x: It was a softer reed because after, I believe Peterson was, when I started buying reeds from him, he asked me what number you want. I said number. I said number.

I said, did it go by number? He said, yeah. He said, you got one, one and a half, two. He said, one and a half is for beginners and youngsters, you know. And he said, two is for a person that's been playing or two and a half. Then he said, three and three and a half is for a person that likes a real stiff read. So I said, well, let's try a three and a half. And gee, I like it. I can make a better tone with that three and a half. As long as my lip is strong, they say I blow it out my teeth. And so I think as long…
Wouldn't make any difference? If you get a little older, wouldn't make sense?
